conditions.human_role: Brice Dudout obtained the photographs, chose the target, answered a blind reading sheet on doubtful digit shapes (two controls passed) and set the counting rule (#728: sure words only, on cipher words). AI agents transcribed, aligned the decipherment, rebuilt the key and wrote up.

solution.what: Cipher groups of both letters transcribed from the library's photographs (245 + 149 groups); doubtful shapes put on a blind reading sheet: 163 (not 168) and 257 in the 1674 letter.

Key rebuilt from the 1674 letter, deciphered group by group between the lines (149 pairs), then extended with the 1673 letter, deciphered word by word: 90 groups, 61 sure, 27 single, 2 inferred. Same key in both letters.

The table is approximately alphabetical (a = 55 ... z = 316, whole words filed by initial letter; inversions 103/104, 159/163, 106-108/109-113, 257): 208 = o, 293 = vo and 74 = ca are inferred from this order (208 counts the struck-through {avoit}; for 293 the decipherer wrote no). The six discordant readings of the decipherer (153, 159, 99, 221, 228, 293) are settled by the words.
Both letters aligned word by word and counted under rule #728: 163 cipher words, 161 sure, 2 probable ({avoit}, {casaque}, in the passage struck through by the decipherer), 0 restored, 0 unresolved.
catalogue.json, research/leads.json, targets and open pull requests searched for Gourjault, Bréant, Baluze, Réveillon, Sedan: nothing; web search: no edition of the decipherment.

outcome.method_basis: Both letters carry a contemporary interlinear decipherment, which gives the text; the 90-group approximately alphabetical nomenclator in key.tsv was rebuilt here from it and checked word by word against it. No new reading is claimed.
outcome.fraction_read_source: decryption files: 163 cipher words, 161 sure (decipherer, key and context agree: agreement with the contemporary gloss plus sense, not an independent test of the key), 2 probable, 0 restored, 0 unresolved; sure words only (rule #728).

texts.label: Bréant to Réveillon, Cologne, 26 Dec 1673
texts.summary: The French plenipotentiaries at Cologne want to know whether Réveillon can hold Kaiserswerth with his French and Swiss troops, with Germans inside the place, in case the Elector of Cologne turns his coat and listens to the Emperor; the matter is to stay between Chamilly, Réveillon and Bréant.
texts.note: Existing: the contemporary decipherment, checked word by word against the rebuilt key. 96 cipher words: 94 sure, 2 probable, 0 restored, 0 unresolved.

texts.label: Bréant to Réveillon, Cologne, 8 Jan 1674
texts.summary: The ambassadors assure Réveillon he will be informed of everything: the Elector of Cologne has promised to listen to no proposal from the Emperor until he has the King's answer to a letter he is sending by a gentleman of his chamber.
texts.note: Existing: the contemporary decipherment, checked group by group against the rebuilt key. 67 cipher words, all sure.
